messages:
Alex Gomez: Hey team — onboarding Q. I missed the domestic partner option when I enrolled 2024-09-02. I live with my partner and want to add them to medical + commuter pre-tax transit. The portal only listed spouse/child. What docs do I need and how will this affect my paycheck (esp taxes)?

Priya (People Ops): Welcome, Alex! We do allow domestic partners. Required docs: signed domestic partner affidavit + one proof of shared residence (lease, bank stmt, utility) dated within 90 days OR a state/city domestic partnership registry certificate if you have one. DM me if you want the PDF. For commuter/transit, we can add mid-cycle but subject to payroll cutoff.

Maya (Benefits): Adding: send docs to benefits@redwood.com with subject line like `DP + RETRO` if you want retro to 2024-09-02. Note that if your partner is not a tax dependent, employer-paid portion of medical is generally taxable (imputed income). That shows up as imputed income on your pay and W-2. If you want to avoid surprises, ask us to estimate the monthly imputed amount before we process.

Alex Gomez: Ah — I didn't realize about imputed income. How big is the hit typically? And for commuter pre-tax, is adding partner allowed?

Maya (Benefits): Imputed income varies by plan tier. For example as a rough ballpark, employer's contribution for 2-person coverage can show as $200-500/mo taxable income depending on plan. We can run an exact estimate once we know the plan tier. Commuter pre-tax is individual, not dependent-based, so you can enroll in transit benefit separately — adding your partner doesn't affect commuter eligibility.

Alex Gomez: Makes sense. My first paycheck already ran. If we do retro to 9/2, will payroll take a big catch-up and also add the imputed income retro?

Priya (People Ops): Tagging @PayrollBot to confirm proration and handling of imputed income for domestic partners. Payroll cutoff is 3pm PT two business days before payday FYI.

PayrollBot: PayrollBot: For retro enrollments approved by carriers, payroll will calculate prorated premiums and imputed income for the retro period. Standard behavior: we can split the catch-up deductions across the next 1-3 pay periods on request to reduce immediate impact. Imputed income is applied in the pay period when enrollment is processed (can be retro-calculated for tax reporting), and will appear on the W-2 for the calendar year. If employer-paid retro premium is billed by carrier directly, Benefits coordinates reimbursements.

Alex Gomez: OK thanks. My partner has COBRA until 2024-09-20. Should I enroll now or wait?

Maya (Benefits): Enroll now and include COBRA docs in the email (subject `DP + RETRO + COBRA`). We'll confirm carrier effective date. If new coverage starts before COBRA end, COBRA can be terminated. We'll help avoid double-billing but timely docs are important.

Alex Gomez: Uploaded affidavit + lease + COBRA notice to benefits@redwood.com with subject `DP + RETRO + COBRA`. Also can you send me the imputed income estimate before processing?

BenefitsAdminBot: BenefitsAdminBot: Received upload. We'll validate docs within 48 hours. Maya will reply with an imputed income estimate and whether carrier allows retro to 2024-09-02.

Maya (Benefits): Got it Alex 0 I'll run the estimate and post it here before we submit to carrier. If you prefer, we can request splitting any catch-ups across next 2 pays.

Alex Gomez: Appreciate it  please split if possible. Thanks everyone! :slightly_smiling_face:
